newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close sharply higher.

text.p: Israeli shares resumed their rally on Sunday after just one day of profit-taking at the end of last week, traders said.

The Tel Aviv stock exchange's benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 2.05 percent, or 4.56 points, to 232.26 on all-share turnover of 170 million shekels against 133 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.15 percent higher at 240.66.
"These are the signals of a recovering market. One key is consistency -- more days when the market goes up than days of profit-taking," said Eran Goren of Zannex Securities.
"I think we'll see a more moderate incline with intervals of profit taking but with volume consistently staying above 100 million shekels a day," he said.
Shachar Gazit of Betucha Securities was more cautious.
"Whenever you expect profit-taking it never comes. It's just a continuation of the trend. It's not like there's any big news," he said.
The most active share was Leumi Insurance Holdings, which soared 81.3 percent percent in its first day trading to 233 agorot on a turnover of 29.4 million shekels.
Shareholders of African Israel Investments received shares in Leumi Insurance as part of a multi-faceted transaction in which Italian insurer Generali is buying control of Leumi Insurance.

The number two most active was Bank Leumi, which gained 3.75 percent to 515 agorot on volume of 6.5 million shekels. Number three Israel Chemicals gained 1.5 percent to 321 agorot on a volume of six million shekels.
